A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BRIDGE and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–N. Corresponding content can be matched reliably across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V3 reports original generation, controllability, forecasting, human-evaluation, and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains original empirical results and reports additional prototype-count results and replacement controllability measurements.

M1.justification: The multi-agent template-refinement procedure, prototype-conditioned diffusion architecture, training objective, and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. Removing role descriptions and dialogue examples does not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 12 in-domain generation datasets, Stock/Web unseen domains, AirPassenger/Sunspots text-refinement tasks, and ILI/M4 downstream forecasting coverage. Additional prototype counts change configurations, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain TimeVQVAE, TimeGAN, GT-GAN, TimeVAE, the BRIDGE variants, and the same text-generation and forecasting comparators. KernelSynth, random-data, and real-data comparisons are retained. Newly cited works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1.3 and 5.3 replace MSE/MAE with J-FTSD for controllability across all 14 generation datasets. Appendix E changes the reported training batch size from 256 to 128 while retaining 50,000 steps, and Appendix K extends the prototype sweep to 32 and 64. These are reported protocol changes; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix K extends the existing 4/8/16-prototype sensitivity analysis to 32 and 64, testing benefits beyond the default of 16. V3's worked agent-dialogue case in Appendix A.6 and Tables 7–10 is removed. The other text-type, encoder, and prototype-visualization analyses remain.

E5.justification: Table 1's uncertainty reporting, averaging across human annotators, and Appendix M's t-tests and 1,000 bootstrap resamples for OWA are retained. V3 Table 18 becomes v4 Table 14 with the same significance threshold and outcomes. No new seed or repeated-run reporting is introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 3–4 replace the quantitative controllability results with J-FTSD measurements; BRIDGE's Stock MSE/MAE of 17.53/32.55 is replaced by J-FTSD 7.483, not a comparable performance gain. Appendix K adds 32/64-prototype results and revises 16-prototype Temperature MDD from 0.310 to 0.356 and Exchange from 0.315 to 0.376. Appendix J revises Wind no-text MDD from 0.319 to 0.304. Main fidelity and downstream forecasting table values are otherwise retained.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, denoising objective, prototype-mask definition, and cross-attention equations are unchanged. J-FTSD is introduced as an empirical metric without a new mathematical definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies the controllability benefit from 12.52% MSE and 6.34% MAE to 'up to 12%' and 6%. The text-controlled generation task, multi-agent refinement contribution, hybrid prototype framework, and 11-of-12-datasets fidelity claim remain.

C2.justification: V4 adds a rationale for J-FTSD and replaces the unseen-domain discussion of ground-truth discrepancies with stronger semantic-alignment and generalization interpretations. It describes text as controlling high-level semantics and prototypes as refining local dynamics. Section 5.6 qualifies prototype benefits beyond 16, while Appendix J removes a dataset-specific caveat about text.

D1.justification: V4 adds a Microsoft/TimeCraft code-access link and revises the documented batch size. Its rewritten STL/ICL account in Appendix A.8 removes v3 A.9's explicit description of decomposed-image inputs and undecomposed-series text. Hardware, Llama3-8B, learning rate, warm-up, and the default 16 prototypes remain documented.

R1.justification: V4 adds citations to Pöhl et al. (2025), Fan et al. (2024), Deng et al. (2025), and Hou et al. (2024), expanding ECG and diffusion-model context. The central positioning relative to GenG, Time-MMD, and TimeDP remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 makes targeted evaluation and discussion rewrites, removes the separate role inventory and extended dialogue-example section, and trims repetitive appendix discussion. Author/front-matter wording and acknowledgements are updated. Most methodological prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 3–4 replace paired MSE/MAE columns with J-FTSD, and the prototype-count table gains columns. Four dialogue-example tables are removed; retained appendix tables and algorithms are repositioned or renumbered. Front-matter layout and some captions change, while Figures 1–17 retain their content.

improvement.justification: V4 adds useful prototype-sensitivity evidence, a code-access link, and corrections to prose/table mismatches. However, the central J-FTSD replacement lacks computational detail in the PDF, while the abstract retains MSE/MAE controllability gains whose supporting columns were removed. V4 also introduces an incorrect claim of an over-three-point Pedestrian HE difference; Table 3 shows 2.2 versus 3.3. These benefits and new reporting problems prevent a confident judgment of net quality improvement.
